item.statement: Joining lifecycle and RFM rows by visitor_id and product-health rows by account_id does not multiply visitor rows.
item.evidence_of_dependence: LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_pendo__user_lifecycle_segments l USING(visitor_id) LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis r USING(visitor_id) LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics h ON v.account_id=h.account_id
item.alternative: Lifecycle documentation says "a visitor may appear multiple times across accounts"; RFM has visitor-account grain and product health has account-app grain, while this mart requires "exactly one output row per visitor_id".
item.reason: Multiple matches can multiply customer records and combine attributes from different account scopes.

item.statement: Every customer may receive the default next-action recommendation without evaluating the specified action rules.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 'Standard nurturing; Regular check-ins; Content engagement' recommended_next_action
item.alternative: The contract requires ordered recommendations including "Immediate intervention; Executive outreach; Value demonstration" for High Risk customers.
item.reason: Recommendations ignore the customer signals that are supposed to determine intervention.

item.statement: Customer segment classification requires only the first three specified rules before defaulting to Standard Customer.
item.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN l.lifecycle_stage='New User' AND r.rfm_segment='New Customers' THEN 'Fresh Prospect' ELSE 'Standard Customer'
item.alternative: The contract additionally specifies "Rising Star", "Save Immediately", "Rescue Mission", and "Lost Customer" before the default.
item.reason: Entire growth and risk segments cannot appear in the output.

item.statement: Every customer may be assigned Maintenance without evaluating the customer-journey rules.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 'Maintenance' customer_journey_stage
item.alternative: The contract requires ordered "Onboarding", "Growth", "Maturity", "Retention", and "Win-back" rules before Maintenance.
item.reason: The output loses all required distinctions between customer journey stages.

item.statement: Every customer may be assigned Standard LTV without evaluating the predicted-LTV rules.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 'Standard LTV' predicted_ltv_tier
item.alternative: The contract specifies "Very High LTV", "High LTV", "Moderate LTV", and "Low LTV" conditions before the default.
item.reason: The required value and risk distinctions cannot influence predicted lifetime value.

item.statement: The executive dashboard may omit the product-health source and leave all four platform health averages null.
item.evidence_of_dependence: NULL::DOUBLE avg_platform_health_score,NULL::DOUBLE avg_platform_nps,NULL::DOUBLE avg_feature_adoption,NULL::DOUBLE avg_retention_rate
item.alternative: The contract requires account history to be left joined to "intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics", per-account maxima, and platform averages of those metrics.
item.reason: The dashboard omits its required product-health and customer-sentiment inputs.

item.statement: The executive dashboard may always report All Systems Normal without evaluating alert conditions.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 'All Systems Normal' primary_alert_status
item.alternative: The contract requires ordered alerts for account risk, customer satisfaction, growth decline, retention, and customer health before the default.
item.reason: Required business alerts cannot be surfaced regardless of the source metrics.

item.statement: All executive account-risk counts may be zero without classifying the accounts.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 0::BIGINT high_risk_accounts,0::BIGINT medium_risk_accounts,0::BIGINT low_risk_accounts
item.alternative: The contract requires counts of accounts labeled "High/Medium/Low Risk" after applying ordered account-risk rules.
item.reason: No account can contribute to any risk category, including the required Low Risk default.

item.statement: The executive dashboard may report zero seven-day growth and Concerning Decline without calculating the recent and prior seven-day averages.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 0::DOUBLE user_growth_rate_7d,'Concerning Decline' growth_trend_assessment
item.alternative: The contract defines growth as the difference between recent and prior seven-day average daily users divided by the prior average, with classification based on the raw result.
item.reason: Observed user growth cannot change either reported trend output.

item.statement: The overall business health score may remain null without evaluating its weighted formula.
item.evidence_of_dependence: NULL::DOUBLE overall_business_health_score
item.alternative: The contract requires a capped weighted composite of health, NPS, adoption, retention, conversion, and growth, becoming null only when a non-growth component is null.
item.reason: The executive score is an unconditional placeholder rather than a calculated KPI.

item.statement: Historical feature and page joins produce at most one matching row for each usage pair within each final feature-attribute group.
item.evidence_of_dependence: sum(u.ev) ev,sum(u.mins) mins,sum(u.days) days FROM u LEFT JOIN h USING(feature_id) LEFT JOIN p USING(page_id) GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
item.alternative: The contract explicitly allows "Multiple historical rows per feature_id" and says duplicate feature-info rows should leave averages unchanged; this code sums replicated usage before averaging.
item.reason: Historical duplicates can inflate per-user totals and active days and change regular-user classification.

item.statement: Every feature ID in feature-event usage has a matching feature-history row.
item.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT h.feature_id ... FROM u LEFT JOIN h USING(feature_id)
item.alternative: The contract starts from usage and requires a "Left join feature_usage_base to feature_info on feature_id", retaining the usage feature identifier even without metadata.
item.reason: Unmatched usage loses its feature identifier and different unmatched features can be merged.

item.statement: Every feature-account-app group has at least one non-null num_events value when computing feature health.
item.evidence_of_dependence: least(100,count(DISTINCT visitor_id)*2+avg(num_events)*5+count(DISTINCT CAST(occurred_at AS DATE))*3) feature_health_score
item.alternative: The contract states "if there are no non-NULL num_events the score is NULL"; DuckDB's LEAST can return 100 when the other argument is null.
item.reason: An all-null event-count group can receive the maximum score instead of a null score.
